raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Bound packed-Parquet shard readers per DataLoader worker with an eight-entry LRU.

## Trigger and impact

Training from a supported packed-Parquet glob or directory with enough shards and persistent workers causes each worker to retain every visited `ParquetFile`. Descriptor usage grows with shard count until training fails with `Too many open files`.

## Root cause

`GPTSFTPackedParquetDataset._ensure_reader()` cached every opened shard in `_parquet_files`. Row-group cache eviction did not close shard readers; cleanup happened only at dataset teardown.

## Fix

Keep an eight-reader LRU per worker. Cache hits refresh recency; misses evict and close only the least-recently-used reader. This bounds resource retention while preserving recent-shard and row-group reuse.

## Regression evidence

Before the fix:

```text
uv run --active --no-sync python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/data/packing/test_parquet.py::TestPackedParquetDatasetMultiFile::test_persistent_workers_bound_open_shard_readers -q -p no:cacheprovider --tb=short
```

Failed because a worker exhausted the controlled descriptor budget with `Too many open files`.

After the fix:

```text
uv run --active --no-sync python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/data/packing/test_parquet.py::TestPackedParquetDatasetMultiFile::test_persistent_workers_bound_open_shard_readers tests/unit_tests/data/packing/test_parquet.py::TestPackedParquetDatasetMultiFile::test_reader_cache_is_bounded_and_reuses_recent_shards -q -p no:cacheprovider --tb=short
```

`2 passed`.

Adjacent validation:

```text
uv run --active --no-sync python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/data/packing/test_parquet.py tests/unit_tests/data/test_samplers.py -q -p no:cacheprovider --tb=short
git diff --check
uv run --no-sync pre-commit run --all-files
```

`46 passed`; diff check and every pre-commit hook passed.

## Scope

No changes to packed row contents, sampling order, collation, public configuration or API, dependencies, CI, or Megatron-Core. No full-suite, convergence, model-quality, or performance validation is claimed.

nodes.body:
This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.

Pull request vetters can view their responsibilities [here](https://docs.gha-runners.nvidia.com/cpr/vetters).

Contributors can view more details about this message [here](https://docs.gha-runners.nvidia.com/cpr/contributors).

Light review - LGTM with one minor note

The LRU bounding of the open-Parquet reader cache is correct:
- Cache hit pops and re-inserts to mark most-recently-used (parquet.py:305-307).
- Miss at capacity evicts the oldest insertion-ordered entry (parquet.py:309-315).
- The materialized row-group table cache is independent of the reader handle, so eviction cannot invalidate it. No correctness regression.

Minor:
- The eviction path (parquet.py:312-315) closes handle then pf without the best-effort try/except that close() uses (parquet.py:352-363). On the local-file path handle is None (safe), but on the MSC seekable path pf wraps handle, so closing handle first could make pf.close() raise and propagate up through getitem during iteration. Consider guarding it to match close().
- The _ensure_reader docstring no longer reflects the new bounded-LRU behavior; a one-line update would help.

Suggested test cases
- tests/unit_tests/data/packing/test_parquet.py::TestPackedParquetDatasetMultiFile::test_persistent_workers_bound_open_shard_readers
- tests/unit_tests/data/packing/test_parquet.py::TestPackedParquetDatasetMultiFile::test_reader_cache_is_bounded_and_reuses_recent_shards

No perf tests impacted.

I also ran into the issue that was supposed to be fixed in this PR. It has been closed for no apparent reason—are there no plans for a fix?

Beyond the exhaustion of file descriptors, a single reader can leave behind memory roughly the size of the file. Since this is outside the Arrow memory pool, it doesn't show up in `pa.total_allocated_bytes()`. As a result, the `DataLoader` worker may be killed during prolonged SFT. I would appreciate it if you could consider fixing this.

@@ -47,6 +47,7 @@
 
 # Required columns in packed Parquet schema
 REQUIRED_COLUMNS = {"input_ids", "seq_start_id", "loss_mask"}
+_MAX_OPEN_PARQUET_FILES = 8
 
 
 def _lazy_import_pyarrow():
@@ -301,7 +302,17 @@ def _ensure_reader(self, file_idx: int):
         survives DataLoader worker forking (each worker creates its own readers).
         """
         if file_idx in self._parquet_files:
-            return self._parquet_files[file_idx][0]
+            pf, handle = self._parquet_files.pop(file_idx)
+            self._parquet_files[file_idx] = (pf, handle)
+            return pf
+
+        if len(self._parquet_files) >= _MAX_OPEN_PARQUET_FILES:
+            oldest_file_idx = next(iter(self._parquet_files))
+            pf, handle = self._parquet_files.pop(oldest_file_idx)
+            if handle is not None:
+                handle.close()
+            if hasattr(pf, "close"):
+                pf.close()
 
         pyarrow, pq = _lazy_import_pyarrow()
         parquet_path = self._parquet_paths[file_idx]

@@ -21,6 +21,7 @@
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
+import resource
 from pathlib import Path
 from unittest.mock import MagicMock
 
@@ -36,6 +37,7 @@
     _resolve_parquet_paths,
     is_packed_parquet_file,
 )
+from megatron.bridge.data.samplers import build_pretraining_data_loader
 
 
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@@ -79,6 +81,12 @@ def _write_parquet(path: str | Path, rows: list[dict], row_group_size: int = 500
     pq.write_table(table, str(path), row_group_size=row_group_size)
 
 
+def _limit_worker_file_descriptors(_worker_id: int) -> None:
+    """Apply a deterministic low descriptor limit inside a DataLoader worker."""
+    _, hard_limit = resource.getrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE)
+    resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE, (min(48, hard_limit), hard_limit))
+
+
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 # Tests: write_packed_parquet
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@@ -272,6 +280,41 @@ def test_locate_row_boundaries(self, multi_parquet):
         assert file_idx_5 == 1
         assert file_idx_15 == 2
 
+    def test_persistent_workers_bound_open_shard_readers(self, tmp_path):
+        for shard_id in range(96):
+            _write_parquet(tmp_path / f"shard_{shard_id:03d}.idx.parquet", [_make_packed_row(n_tokens=16, n_seqs=1)])
+        dataset = _make_dataset(str(tmp_path / "shard_*.idx.parquet"))
+        data_loader = build_pretraining_data_loader(
+            dataset,
+            consumed_samples=0,
+            dataloader_type="single",
+            micro_batch_size=1,
+            num_workers=2,
+            data_sharding=True,
+            worker_init_fn=_limit_worker_file_descriptors,
+            collate_fn=dataset.collate_fn,
+            persistent_workers=True,
+        )
+
+        batches = list(data_loader)
+
+        assert len(batches) == len(dataset)
+
+    def test_reader_cache_is_bounded_and_reuses_recent_shards(self, tmp_path):
+        for shard_id in range(12):
+            _write_parquet(tmp_path / f"shard_{shard_id:03d}.idx.parquet", [_make_packed_row(n_tokens=16, n_seqs=1)])
+        dataset = _make_dataset(str(tmp_path / "shard_*.idx.parquet"))
+
+        dataset[0]
+        first_reader = dataset._parquet_files[0][0]
+        dataset[1]
+        dataset[0]
+
+        assert dataset._parquet_files[0][0] is first_reader
+        for index in range(len(dataset)):
+            dataset[index]
+        assert len(dataset._parquet_files) <= 8
+
 
 class TestPackedParquetDatasetRowGroupCache:
     """Tests for row-group caching behavior."""
